# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 31 THE TRUTH MAKES FREE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Once Lorna had determined her course, she carried it out with her typical speed and determination. No matter what matters of life or death were waiting outside, cleaning the house had to be completed before anything else. With prompt aid from Miss Winifred, the gray house located up the brook was restored to immaculate cleanliness and order. Having voiced her mind to Nell, and subsequently to Hugh and Captain Saul—without holding back from either, rest assured—Miss Winifred refrained from ever discussing the issue with Lorna. Accepting the reality of Rufus’s surgery, she brought it up in a practical manner whenever required, and disregarded it otherwise. Lorna made no effort to speak about it. Throughout those lovely spring days, she remained extremely distant and silent. Her visits to Nell were infrequent, and despite her constant politeness and friendliness, that precise civility formed a frozen wall separating her from the inhabitants of the small house. The former jests, mirth, and easy familiarity over everyday matters were unable to touch her across that divide. Nell declined to take offense. She recognized that Lorna was held fast by a gruesome fear—a fear that isolated her from every small moment of joy and time of delight. Whenever a single grand emotion dominates the spirit, every other emotion is pushed to the side. At no point in her existence had Lorna Vane recoiled from what was to come with such unbearable horror. Yet, she advanced along her chosen track as steadfastly as the ancient martyrs trod their selected path, fully aware that its conclusion was the burning anguish of the stake.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0000 }

Resolving the monetary issue proved less difficult than Nell had anticipated. From Captain Saul, Lorna obtained the required funds, and because she demanded it, he accepted a mortgage upon the small farm.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0001 }

“With that settled, the poor girl has one less burden on her mind,” Miss Winifred remarked to Nell, “and so do I. Provided Rufus recovers sufficiently to resume working, his earnings will cover the interest payments; should he fail to do so, I am certain Captain Saul will find a way to spare Lorna from that obligation. He practically admitted it to me. 'Winifred, my years are advancing,’ he stated, 'and I lack any offspring. While Lorna would refuse a present from someone who is alive, she might accept it from someone who has passed away.’ Therefore, that particular matter will turn out fine. If only every other issue could be resolved just as smoothly. Regarding that miserable Rufus, his behavior over the past few days has been terrible. You must take my word for it, he was possessed! His antics prevented Lorna and me from accomplishing our chores. On one occasion, he ran her ducks all over the yard until the majority of them perished. Furthermore, he refused to assist us in any way. Occasionally, as you are aware, he renders himself rather useful by carrying in firewood and buckets of water. This past week, however, sending him to the well resulted in his attempting to descend inside it. At one point I pondered, 'If you were to simply plunge down there head-first, all our problems would be neatly resolved.’”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0002 }

“Ah, Miss Winifred!”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0003 }

“Now, you don't need to call me Miss Winifred, my dear Nell. EVERYONE would have come to the identical conclusion. Should the physicians in Montreal succeed in transforming Rufus Vane into a sensible person, they are truly remarkable.”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0004 }

At the beginning of May, Lorna traveled to Montreal with Rufus. Accompanying her was Hugh, who wanted to assist her and handle her required preparations. Upon returning home, he reported that the Montreal surgeon they had seen shared his view regarding the high probability of Rufus’s recovery.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0005 }

“Very comforting,” Miss Winifred remarked sarcastically.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0006 }

A sigh was all that came from Nell. During their farewell, Lorna had acted extremely detached.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0007 }

Yet she had given her word that she would send a letter. The missive arrived ten days following the return of Hugh. Within it, Lorna stated that the surgical procedure had been carried out with success and that Rufus was recovering well.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0008 }

“What is her meaning when she uses 'successfully?’” Nell inquired. “Is she implying that the restoration of Rufus’s memory has truly occurred?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0009 }

“Unlikely—given that she omits any mention of it,” Hugh remarked. “The term 'successfully’ is employed by her through the eyes of the surgeon. Having been executed, the procedure yielded standard outcomes. Nevertheless, determining if Rufus’s senses will ultimately be brought back, completely or partially, remains premature. A sudden recovery of his memory would not be expected. Should it happen whatsoever, the progression is going to be step-by-step. Does her account end there?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0010 }

“Yes—that is her letter. Its length is very brief. Poor girl, the strain she is experiencing must be terrible. Hugh Carrow, I desire to say a great number of things to you, except that doing so would be mean.”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0011 }

“Miss Winifred utters them on your behalf,” Hugh remarked, smiling ruefully. “Every time I cross her path, she gives me a dressing-down. She leaves no doubt in my mind that she considers me hardly superior to a killer, and that she deems it a terrible shame Dr. Dave permitted me to take over his practice. She went so far as to tell me that the Methodist doctor across the harbor ought to be chosen over me. In Miss Winifred's eyes, the intensity of disapproval can reach no higher peak.”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0012 }

“Should Winifred Tolley fall ill, Doctor Dave and the Methodist physician are not the ones she would call upon,” Tabitha sniffed. “It is you who would be dragged from your well-deserved sleep during the night, doctor, dear, were she to suffer a fit of distress, indeed she would. Afterward, she would probably claim your charge exceeded all fairness. Yet pay her no attention, doctor, dear. Every type of person is required to form a world.”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0013 }

For a period after this, not a single message arrived from Lorna. As the days of May slipped slowly past in a delightful sequence, green plants, flowers, and purple shades covered the coast of Seven Gulls Harbor. During the latter part of May, Hugh returned home on a certain day, and Tabitha was waiting to meet him in the stable yard.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0014 }

“Doctor, dear, I fear that Mrs. Doctor is troubled by something,” she remarked with an air of secrecy. “A letter arrived for her this afternoon, and ever since, she has done nothing but wander about the garden while speaking to herself. Doctor, dear, you are aware that spending so much time standing is bad for her. She chose not to reveal her news to me, and doctor, dear, I am not a curious person and never have been, but she is clearly disturbed. And being disturbed is bad for her.”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0015 }

Hugh made his way to the garden with a good deal of anxiety. Was something wrong at Grey Shutters? Sitting on the rustic seat near the brook, Nell did not appear distressed, however, even though she was undoubtedly very agitated. Her eyes had turned their deepest gray, and bright red patches glowed upon her cheeks.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0016 }

“What has occurred, Nell?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0017 }

Nell uttered a strange, quiet chuckle.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0018 }

“You will scarcely trust my words when I share this, Hugh. It still seems unbelievable to me. Just as Tabitha remarked recently, 'I feel like a fly coming to live in the sun—dazed-like.’ Everything is so beyond belief. Twenty times I have gone through the letter, yet each reading yields the same result—my eyes cannot be trusted. Oh, Hugh, you proved to be correct—entirely correct. That is obvious enough to me at present—and my self-reproach is so deep—and can you truly pardon me ever?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0019 }

“Nell, unless you become clear, I’ll shake you. You ought to make Wexcombe ashamed. WHAT is the matter?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0020 }

“It is unbelievable—it is unbelievable—”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0021 }

“I shall call Uncle Dave on the telephone,” Hugh remarked, feigning a movement toward the house.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0022 }

“Take a seat, Hugh. I will attempt to explain it to you. A letter has arrived, and oh, Hugh, the whole thing is so astonishing—so unbelievably astonishing—we never imagined—not a single one of us ever conceived—”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0023 }

“In a situation like this, taking a seat with an resigned expression, the sole course of action, I presume,” Hugh remarked, “is to remain patient and address the issue step by step. Who sent you that letter?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0024 }

“Lorna—and, ah, Hugh—”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0025 }

“Lorna! Wow! What does she have to report? What is the update regarding Rufus?”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0026 }

Nell picked up the letter and offered it, displaying a calm sense of drama in an instant.
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0027 }

“Rufus does NOT exist! The individual whom we assumed to be Rufus Vane—and who all the people in Seven Gulls have accepted as Rufus Vane for twelve years—is actually his cousin, Laurence Vane, from Nova Scotia, a man who, as it turns out, constantly bore a remarkable resemblance to him. Rufus Vane passed away from yellow fever in Cuba thirteen years ago.”
{: #nw-v04-c31-p0028 }
